propositions: The complexity lock compares branch ceilings against main tip rather than merge-base, causing false violations when main lowers a ceiling and un-rebased branches still carry the pre-reduction baseline
Every future ceiling reduction on main will break the entire fleet of un-rebased branches identically, defeating the purpose of the shrink-only ratchet
The merge-base fetch uses --depth=1 which is too shallow to compute merge bases on diverged branches
Un-rebased branches carrying pre-reduction baselines must pass the lock when compared against the merge-base, while branches that genuinely raise or add new entries must still fail
When merge-base computation fails, the gate must fall back to main-tip comparison with explicit notification, never silently passing genuine ceiling raises
